newsitem.title: UK: Tight North Sea, buying leads to firmer levels.
newsitem.headline: Tight North Sea, buying leads to firmer levels.

text.p: Differentials on the remaining cargoes of July loading North Sea sweet crudes were heading higher with Brent leading the way as demand outstripped supply, traders said.

Two Brent cargoes were bought by one company and expected to be kept for their own use but price details on these July 12-14 cargoes were not divulged. Market talk put the deals around August Brent -12 to August -8 cents.
One refiner offering two later Brent cargoes was heard at August parity. Although many felt this was above refining value, they predicted the next deal would be around August -5 cents.
"The market is short. There's no Iraqi crude and, although everyone is pointing to refining margins they are not that bad at all," one trader said.
Although some argued that the hype had been overdone and had panicked some refiners into bidding for barrels, no one argued that current differentials would not hold in the short term.

August Brent on the IPE gained some 19 cents to trade at $18.70 by 1740 GMT. Traders said the rise was partly attributable to the draw in U.S. crude stocks expected to show up in the figures from the API due out later tonight.
CFD values shot up after a July/August Brent was heard to have traded at +10 cents. The spread traded at a low of -11 cents on Monday but ended Monday with a -2.5 cent value.
Bids at +10 cents on July/August met offers at +20 cents. Brent Aug/Sept talked around -3 cents.
"The market is tight enough but these levels are overdone," one trader said, commenting on the upward move of more than 20 cents on the July/Aug spread.
Brokers valued the remainder of this week (July 1-4) around evens with August while July 7-11 talked Aug -4/-1 cent after trading between -9 cents and -1 cent over the day.
